source.citation: 'Mr. Marshall Field's House' (text headed 'Marshall Field's House.'), pp. 43-47 in Artistic Houses: Being a Series of Interior Views of a Number of the Most Beautiful and Celebrated Homes in the United States, with a Description of the Art Treasures Contained Therein, vol. 2, part 1 (New York: printed for the subscribers by D. Appleton and Company, MDCCCLXXXIV), with two plates, 'Hall' and 'Library'.
what_it_does_not_supply: the yard in 1904: it is twenty years earlier
the number, species or places of the shade-trees
any flower bed, walk or fence outdoors: the flowers it names are inside the conservatory
any dimension of the lawn, the conservatory or the stables
what_it_supplies: an open south yard by 1883-84: 'a spacious lawn and scattered shade-trees' on the southern side
the conservatory on the south side, opening from the reception-room and the dining-room, with plants and an indoor fountain
the stables and other out-buildings at the rear, on the lake (east) side
the porte-cochere on the north side and the entrance in the centre of the west front, up granite steps
red pressed brick with light sandstone trim, three storeys
